# Urdyn Memory Engine

> A local-first, persistent, structured, model-independent memory engine for humans, AI systems, and agents.

Urdyn stores project knowledge (decisions, root causes, verified lessons, evidence, conflicts) in a local, canonical, append-preserving store, independent of any particular AI model or provider. It distinguishes Evidence (what was observed) from Memory (what is believed), and compiles task-aware working context on demand rather than exposing an ever-growing dump. The base engine requires no LLM and no cloud service; semantic (embedding-based) retrieval is an optional, separately installed extra.

## Documentation

- [README](README.md): English overview, installation, and quick start.
- [Italian README](README.it.md): Italian documentation, semantically equivalent to the English README.

## Package

- [Python source](src/urdyn/): the `urdyn` package (also installs a `urdyn` CLI).
- [Tests](tests/): behavioral and regression tests.

## Key concepts

- **Canonical memory** — durable, typed records (`decision`, `lesson`, `root_cause`, `invariant`, `note`, and more) that can be superseded or invalidated but never silently rewritten.
- **Evidence** — an observation (command output, test result, user confirmation, file content, ...) a memory can cite as support. A memory is only `verified` when backed by evidence of a kind strong enough to justify it.
- **Context compiler** — given a task description, retrieves and compiles relevant memories, lessons, and Project Evidence into a single budgeted working context (`urdyn context`). Large seeded documents contribute task-relevant portions rather than having to fit as a whole.
- **Generic export** — a portable, task-scoped compiled context suitable for piping into another tool or prompt (`urdyn export`); not a full memory-archive export.
- **Seed** — records existing project files as Source/Evidence observations (`urdyn seed`); explicit paths work in every profile, while no-path discovery is a `dev` feature. Seeded content can participate in lexical and optional semantic context retrieval as Project Evidence, but remains document evidence rather than verified Memory; retrieval never promotes it to Memory.
